title: Ex 2.6 #5 · ∼(P ∨ Q ∨ R) = (∼P) ∧ (∼Q) ∧ (∼R)
prompt: Use a truth table to show that $\sim (P \vee Q \vee R)$ and $(\sim P) \wedge (\sim Q) \wedge (\sim R)$ are logically equivalent: they have the same truth value in every row.
answer_format: No final answer box. Give the truth-table column of each statement as a column step (statement : T F T T, rows (P, Q, R) in the order TTT, TTF, TFT, TFF, FTT, FTF, FFT, FFF), or rewrite one statement into the other with expr steps, each equivalent to the one before.
hints: P ∨ Q ∨ R is false in only one row. Which one?
solution: $P \vee Q \vee R$ is false only in the last row (all three false), so $\sim (P \vee Q \vee R)$ is F F F F F F F T.
$(\sim P) \wedge (\sim Q) \wedge (\sim R)$ is true only when $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are all false: F F F F F F F T.
The columns agree in every row, so the statements are logically equivalent. This extends DeMorgan's law to three statements.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
